checklist.evidence: Reviewed all 92 paths enumerated by specs/verifications/e06-review-round11-source.json: 24 first-party code/test paths, eight first-party documentation/manifest paths and 60 vendored paths. Reviewed-path inventories were recorded in incremental sections.

Cargo.toml patches crossterm to vendor/crossterm; Cargo.lock selects 0.29.0. Reviewed all six declared changed vendor files and the integration context of the other 54. Release identity is based on sealed-manifest provenance, not an independently fetched baseline.

src/daemon.rs:294–486 validates mutually exclusive profile/raw launch forms and bounded absolute argv. src/acp.rs:1370–1407 invokes Command::new with separate arguments and explicit cwd, without shell interpolation.

src/acp_profiles.rs:116–192 resolves executable files through absolute PATH directories without canonicalizing away the invocation path. Missing executables fail explicitly. tests/acp/profiles.rs covers absolute and PATH symlink invocation identity.

src/cli.rs separates native attaching launch from an explicitly supplied controller. src/tui/control.rs registers an original attachment controller and submits one acp-open on its worker; daemon launch reserves and publishes target authority together.

src/acp_profiles.rs:11–51 rejects duplicate JSON option keys and preserves exact strings. src/cli.rs:203–249 supports delimiter-containing identities through options JSON. src/tui/launch.rs rejects oversized/control-containing edits in full rather than launching truncated settings.

src/projects.rs separates disk schemas from runtime state, validates profile patches before persistence and restores the previous configuration on save failure. Runtime ACP instances, grants and sessions are not persisted.

src/acp/settings.rs validates only model, mode, effort and options with existing identifier/content limits. src/acp_profiles.rs bounds profile count, labels and argv; src/acp.rs validates requested settings before reserving a runtime instance.

src/acp/settings.rs:290–345 resolves semantic settings only through advertised models, modes and configuration categories. Explicit option IDs remain distinct; ambiguous or unsupported semantic requests fail rather than selecting guessed alternatives.

src/acp/settings.rs:346–442 serializes original setting requests, requires confirming configOptions responses and checks final applied values. src/acp.rs:1920–1951 advances configuration before ready; prompt admission requires lifecycle ready.

checklist.area: Truthful settings and permission policy presentation
checklist.evidence: Configuration projections distinguish requested, reported, agent-default, applied, changed and failed states. src/tui/agent.rs and src/tui/launch.rs explicitly avoid interpreting mode metadata or unreported defaults as permission guarantees.

src/acp.rs validates notification, form and permission tool-call identities using the separate 4-KiB tool ID bound. Local session/settings/RPC identifier limits remain separate; original tool IDs are retained rather than shortened or replaced.

src/daemon.rs:490–514 authorizes control before preparing a mutation and commits through Authority::admit_acp. The narrow unchanged src/control.rs:1194–1253 reference rechecks exact current owner/reference/generation while holding target authority across commit.

checklist.area: Force does not interrupt or kill
checklist.evidence: The unchanged registry force branch supersedes reservation and grants authority without invoking ACP cancellation or process cleanup. Native Force requires presented confirmation and current captured observations; broker interrupt and close remain separate explicit actions.

Reviewed claim controls and first-party regressions, including tests/acp/native/recovery_edges.rs:735–760. Pending cancellation leaves owner/reservation empty while exact retained broker work and process identity remain intact; it does not select an answer or interrupt the turn.

src/tui/control.rs:1178–1329 queues explicit keep before subsequent application activity on the original FIFO. Reviewed unchanged registry controls and tests/pty_control/native.rs conditional cases preserving the human token and preventing automatic external-policy rearming.

src/tui.rs routes key, literal prefix, paste and application mouse input through NativeControl. src/tui/control.rs:894–940 checks connection/current control and rejects PTY forwarding for ACP targets. ACP editor events have no raw-PTY fallback.

checklist.area: Captured drafts and no automatic replay
checklist.evidence: src/tui/agent.rs binds first edits to exact target/control/generation, discards mismatched drafts and returns captured action envelopes. Definite non-admission may restore only the original binding for a deliberate new submission; uncertain transport does not trigger retry.

src/acp.rs:2076–2275 correlates local interaction/revision to its retained original wire responder and validates session or outstanding request scope. Form responses use that exact request ID; parent RPC completion does not silently replace or cancel the responder.

src/acp.rs:897–931 and 2277–2315 permit only offered option IDs on the exact pending interaction/session. $/cancel_request withdrawal is ordered under the same state lock and cannot replace an admitted human response. tests/acp/omp.rs:308–430 checks exact denial and stale-response rejection.

src/tui.rs:817–856 validates the original daemon_id. Recovery connects only to the existing socket and does not call ensure_daemon. A replaced daemon or missing original target produces an ended attachment rather than relaunch or same-name substitution.

Resume validation preserves id, instance_id, connection_generation and every established session_id. Only initial null-to-established session identity may advance. Acknowledged launches retain their own exact continuity target across follow-up observation loss.

src/tui/control.rs:162–327 checks both authority and observation sockets plus heartbeat before dequeuing work, and rechecks after compound claim observation. src/tui.rs checks pause/connection state and stops old authority before cleanup or recovery.

src/tui.rs:1280–1394 keeps recovery input discard-only until a painted observer frame, conclusive empty input boundary and reconciled geometry. Fresh controller provenance disables automatic acquisition; queued claim/consent/Force gestures are not replayed.

vendor/crossterm/src/event.rs:206–239 exposes Empty/Pending/Inconclusive. src/event/read.rs:44–81 skips bounded internal replies, preserves public events and requires a source exhaustion proof. TUI safety boundaries use this API rather than interpreting filtered poll(false) as emptiness.

vendor/crossterm/src/event/source/unix/mio.rs:81–205 retains parser fragments, caps work at 32 visits and allows the initial zero-deadline readiness visit without indefinite drain. A bounded yield or incomplete sequence does not certify Empty.

The mio source finishes retained token batches before further TTY parsing and performs level readiness checks before reads. It does not set shared parent-shell O_NONBLOCK flags. The terminal Unix helpers retain raw-mode restoration. Focused regression sources cover sustained incomplete input and recovery geometry.

src/acp.rs sanitizes narrative/tool display content; src/tui/agent.rs bounds and escapes controls/bidi at rendering while retaining canonical response values. Wrapper labels are clipped safely. Native PTY rendering consumes parsed terminal cells, not raw child escape streams.

src/acp.rs:398–520 marks unresolved work/interactions unknown on closure, retains independent submitted/write-failed evidence and protects pending/in-flight responders from completed-history eviction. Delivery is not treated as application acknowledgement or safe native settlement.

src/acp.rs:1241–1533 owns the original child/session, birth-qualified process tree, cancellable pipe endpoints and joined workers. Cleanup checks reaping, descendants, joins and endpoint closure; process-identity or cleanup uncertainty remains observable and charged.

Profile catalogs omit argv/environment; default public metadata omits conversation content and private capability handles. Adapter stderr is bounded rather than published as raw diagnostics. tests/acp/native/omp_live.rs uses private spec checks and category-only failure output without formatting provider content or auth.

Reviewed settled E06 scope/threat model, PLAN.md lines 1–45, README/changelog and regression sources for all three stories. Fixtures are identified as protocol evidence and genuine-provider acceptance remains explicitly ignored/opt-in. Historical native unknown settlement, exhausted caps and failed live acceptance are not converted into success by source approval.

summary: Static E06 source/security review PASS: 32/32 checklist items, score 100. All 92 frozen paths were reviewed, with focused tracing of the six modified vendor files and their authority-sensitive consumers. No supported Must-fix, Should-fix or optional security finding survived source-to-consumer analysis. This is source approval only, not installed-provider or end-to-end acceptance.
limits: Read-only static analysis only. No edits, builds, tests, lint, formatting, shell/source execution, payload execution, network/provider calls, auth/config/daemon/global operations or commits were performed. No previous reviews, audits, runtime reports, saved handoff/state, execution logs or real auth/private retired fixtures were read; PLAN.md was restricted to lines 1–45. Narrow unchanged control/runtime references were used only to resolve causal consumers. Branch/base and vendor baseline identity rely on the sealed manifest; frozen hashes were not recomputed and upstream release files were not fetched. Runtime scheduling, platform behavior, actual installed OMP same-instance question/permission effects, provider budgets and complete cleanup were not exercised. Fixture coverage and ignored live tests do not establish installed-provider acceptance. Historical unsafe native application settlement and live-acceptance failures/caps remain unchanged and unwaived.
